For time and space requirements, the answer to such questions is given by the time and space hierarchy theorems respectively. The **time hierarchy theorem** and the **space hierarchy theorem** are responsible for determining questions of time and space requirements, respectively.

- The **time hierarchy theorem** shows that for any time-constructible function f(n), there are problems that can be solved in time O(f(n)) but not in time o(f(n)/log f(n)). This establishes a strict hierarchy among time-bounded complexity classes such as DTIME(f(n)) and DTIME(g(n)), where g(n) grows faster than f(n).

- The **space hierarchy theorem** similarly shows that for any space-constructible function f(n), there are problems that can be solved using O(f(n)) space but not O(f(n)/log f(n)) space, establishing a strict hierarchy among space-bounded complexity classes such as DSPACE(f(n)) and DSPACE(g(n)).

These theorems guarantee that increasing the allowed time or space strictly increases the set of solvable problems, thus creating a proper hierarchy among complexity classes based on resource requirements.
